encoder: legalese-sonnet-5.5-ch3: a single Sonnet 5.5 agent working alone from the brief (BRIEF.md), no other agents
display_name: Swiss Federal Supreme Court Act (BGG, SR 173.110), chapter 3, Art. 72 to 89: the Federal Supreme Court as the ordinary appeal instance, from the German text, L4 stable
maintainer: unassigned (written by the single-agent run dst-bgg3)
seat: a person affected by a decision (a party to civil or criminal proceedings, or to proceedings in a public-law matter, who lost, or a person with another interest the text names), asking on facts they can state whether they may appeal to the Federal Supreme Court, which appeal it is, whether the value in dispute is enough, whether they have standing, which decisions are excluded from appeal, and whether the case must first have gone through the cantons' highest instance

scope.edition: Fedlex consolidated version in German, applicable from 2026-04-01, as the plain-text rendering ch-bgg-sr173110-ch3-art-72-89-20260401.txt (sha256 918277c2175f13e88e2c98b4bbe8ecb4b9c44598538bb54f2ab8b9f13ad3db13); the rendering is not the official text
scope.encoded: all of chapter 3, Art. 72 to 89 (163 units counted from the text: 77 encoded, 59 fork, 24 inert for reason 1, 3 repealed or blank in this text; see the coverage table in NOTES.md)
scope.not_encoded: the headings and the file header (inert, reason 1); three provisions the text shows as repealed (Art 72(2)(b)(7), Art 81(1)(b)(4), Art 83(s)(1)); chapter 4 and following, the Federal Constitution and the other statutes the chapter cites are outside the sources and are asked as inputs
scope.time: as in force; no earlier versions

not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the text. A Swiss lawyer has not reviewed the fork register (F1 to F22) or the marginal readings. The text file is a script-made rendering and is not the official text; nothing here is verified against the official text.

checks.check.sh: L4=<l4 1.6.110> L4_MAIN=<l4 1.6.109> ./check.sh, target main: 13 modules, 0 errors, 681 assertions satisfied, 0 failed, 0 refused on both builds; every module reads the same on 1.6.109
checks.traces: 10 regulative-rule traces in three test files (the stable binary cannot assert a regulative rule); outcomes compared by hand between 1.6.110 and 1.6.109: identical
checks.srcrefs: python3 -I srcrefs.py check --refs and --strict <text> bgg3-*.l4: 388 src lines, 144 runs, 246 locators, 0 problems
checks.quotecheck: python3 -I quotecheck.py <text> bgg3-*.l4 NOTES.md: no quoted fragment missing from the text (re-run 2026-11-18)
checks.coverage: python3 -I coverage.py <text>: COVERAGE OK (226 non-blank lines, each in exactly one of 163 rows)
checks.not_precedence: no unparenthesised NOT before AND/OR in any of the 13 files (35 NOT tokens checked)
checks.seat_polarity: Art 73, Art 79 and Art 83 seat questions are asked as 'is my decision excluded' (JUST TRUE = excluded); see NOTES.md, Seat polarity (independent reader)

independent_review.how: Written by a separate agent from the source text alone, before it opened the encoding; where the text can be read two ways the file's expected value follows the encoding and carries a RECONCILED comment naming both readings, and the triage says which lines those are.

folder_total_check_sh.note: includes the independent file; the encoder's own count, in the checks field, does not

independent_review.seat_polarity: A second independent reader checked each seat question's wording against what JUST TRUE and JUST FALSE mean in the function it calls; what it found and what changed is in NOTES.md, in the section on seat polarity.
